newsitem.title: MOROCCO: FORECAST - Morocco sees GDP at minus 1.0 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Morocco sees GDP at minus 1.0 pct in 1997.

text.p: The Moroccan government forecasts growth of minus 1.0 percent in 1997 due to a drop in agriculture output, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
"On the basis of the climate's negative changes in recent months and the expected drop in agriculture output...we forecast negative growth of around minus 1.0 percent," the official told Reuters.
He said the government was examining details of the 1997/98 budget which will be presented before parliament in May and be effective from July 1, 1997 once adopted by parliament.
But it was too early to give details of the draft.

The Casablanca-based independent Centre Marocain de Conjoncture think-tank earlier said Morocco's economy "may stagnate or drop to minus one percent in 1997, from 11.8 percent growth in 1996, due mainly to the declining trend of agriculture output this year."
Agricultural activity represents nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs 50 percent of the country's estimated 10 million workforce.
The country's GDP jumped to 11.8 percent in 1996 from minus 7.6 percent in 1995. It reached $34.7 billion the same year against $31.8 billion in 1995, the Statistics Directorate said.

In 1995/6 Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals in against 1.6 million tonnes in 1994/95 season after it was hit by a severe drought described by the authorities as "the drought of the century."

The government, which expected the country's GDP to grow at between 3.5 and 4.0 percent this year based on a modest cereals harvest of 7.0 million tonnes, has dramatically revised its deficit forecast, the finance ministry said.

"The government also expects the budget deficit to widen to 3.2 percent in 1997 from the expected 2.8 percent in the same period due to extra spendings including wage increase and commodity subsidies," the ministry added.
Last year the ministry said the budget deficit which was 15 billion dirhams in 1995 or 5.0 percent of GDP, would be reduced to 2.8 percent in 1996/1997.
The 117.1 billion budget in 1996/97 was aimed at structural reforms and boosting economic growth.
